title: Mycobacteria DNA extraction using bead disruption - Manual method
author: Patrick Camp

steps_raw.instruction: Prepare 2ml Sealed screw cap bead beater tubes by adding 200µl ± 100µl of 0.1mm silica beads.
Make 1X TE: Add 500µl of Tris-EDTA Buffer 100X Concentrate + 45.5ml of H20.
Add 400µl of 1X TE into the bead beater tubes with silica beads

Figure the amount of Phenol/Chloroform/Isoamyl alchol (PCI) 25:24:1 (v:v:v) needed per sample (400µl/sample). Place the amount needed in a 50ml conical tube inside a fume hood. Use the 50ml conical tube to add 400µl into the bead beater tubes from step 3.
Turn on centrifuge to cool down to 4°C and place 70% & 100% Ethanol in the -20°C freezer to use at a later step.
Move to appropriate Biological Safety Cabinet and add 2-3 loopfuls of growth from solid media to prepared beat beater tubes with 1X TE and PCI.
Beat the samples at full speed for 2 minutes (depending on machine) using the Beadbeater machine.
Spin samples at 16,000 ± 500 × g for 5 ± 1 minute.
While samples spin add 30μl 3 M sodium acetate buffer solution to a labeled 1.5ml microcentrifuge tube.
Pull samples from the centrifuge.
DNA is contained in the top aqueous layer. Remove this layer, approximately 300μl, by pipetting and add it to the 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube with 3 M sodium acetate buffer solution.
Add 700µl of 100% ice-cold ethanol to the samples. Invert the tubes 10 times and vortex full speed for < 2 seconds.
Cool samples at -80°C for 10-15 minutes (or put in -20°C freezer for 30 min or indefinitely).
Spin at 4 ± 2°C, 16,000 ± 500 × g for 15 ± 1 minute.
Pour off the ethanol and add 1 ml ice-cold 70% ethanol.
Spin at 4 ± 2°C, 16,000 ± 500 × g for 5 ± 1 minute and pour off ethanol.
Spin at 8,000 ± 500 × g for 15 ± 5 seconds, and immediately remove remaining ethanol with a 100 - 200μl pipette. Place tip of pipette on the opposite side from the pellet.
Dry the samples at room temperature with tubes tilted and caps open for 15-20 minutes or until remaining ethanol has evaporated.
Add 300µl of 1X TE buffer. If a small amount of DNA is expected a smaller volume of 1X TE buffer can be used. Scrape the inside of the tube with the pipette tip when resuspending the DNA.
Keep DNA at 4°C for short term storage or -80°C for long term storage.
